The added capabilities provide investors with new visibility

 into the use of PIK loans

, /PRNewswire/ -- Kroll, the leading independent provider of global financial and risk advisory solutions, and StepStone Group (Nasdaq: STEP), a leading global private markets investment firm, have today launched three new payment-in-kind (PIK) indicators within the Kroll StepStone Private Credit Benchmarks, giving lenders, investors and analysts greater visibility into the use of noncash interest across private credit. The indicators cover more than 28,000 direct lending instruments, 18,000 deals and 13,000 borrowers, with historical data extending back to 2012.

The new measures track loans with an active PIK component across the U.S. and Europe as well as across different sectors and obligor-size segments using three distinct metrics:

The data offers a reliable view on the dynamic role that noncash interest plays in private credit markets, including the variance in PIK activity across EBITDA segments, geographies and sectors. For example, the Benchmarks indicate that on a global basis PIK use is currently moderating rather than accelerating. Across loans originated globally during the previous 12 months, PIK represented 2.86% of interest income as of October 10, 2026, compared with 6.67% across the global cohort of outstanding loans at the end of Q2 2026.

Michael H. Dolan, President of Financial Advisory at Kroll says, "Private credit and private capital markets have demonstrated relatively solid fundamentals, despite a prolonged period of higher borrowing costs and economic uncertainty. PIK is an important part of understanding what is happening beneath headline returns in private credit; the distinction between interest paid in cash and interest added to debt matters when assessing liquidity, leverage, credit quality and ultimately value."

"Operating at the intersection of value, risk and transactions gives Kroll a unique perspective on these dynamics. As private markets continue to grow and become increasingly complex, independent data, analysis and expertise become more important in distinguishing isolated pressure from broader market trends, bringing greater clarity and peace of mind to investors."

"The growth and evolution of private credit have created a more diverse market, making it increasingly valuable to understand how financing structures are changing alongside it," says Marcel Schindler, Partner and Head of Private Debt at StepStone Group. "Greater visibility into PIK activity across markets, sectors and borrower sizes provides another dimension for assessing market dynamics, comparing opportunities and understanding how portfolios are evolving over time."

The new indicators are available in the Kroll StepStone Private Credit Benchmarks, with historical data going back to 2012. Find out more or request a demo here.
